old: Long before it named a song, this word could mean people moving in a circle, voices rising together as they turned.
Its Middle English ancestor named a round dance with singing — and, oddly, also a small writing desk or study stall.
It shares distant roots with 'chorus,' both possibly tracing back to a Greek word for a circling dance of singers.
clues: This kind of song once named a round dance, in which a circle of people moved together while singing.
Today it names a joyful Christmas song, often sung by groups going door to door, and usually lighter and more festive than a solemn hymn.
Dickens titled his tale of Scrooge 'A Christmas ___.' In medieval English the word could even mean a writing desk or a small enclosed stall.
